caption: A contest contact on phone, from CQ to log. The runner calls "CQ contest"; you answer once with your call sign. The runner sends the signal report and the contest information — in November Sweepstakes that is report, serial number, precedence code, his call sign, check (the last two digits of the year he was first licensed), and ARRL section — you send yours back, and he closes with "QSL, thanks, K1ZZ, contest," signing off, identifying, and re-calling CQ in three words. The contact goes into the log in UTC. In contests the 59 report is a formality; FCC identification rules still apply, and other contests define other information (ARRL DX: RST + state/province; Field Day: class + section; IARU HF: RST + ITU zone).
spoken: A contest contact: the runner calls C Q contest, and you answer with your call sign, once. In November Sweepstakes the exchange is a signal report, a serial number, a precedence code, the call sign, a check — the year first licensed — and the ARRL section. The runner closes and re-calls C Q in one breath, and the contact goes into the log in U T C.
